object_description: campus of three school buildings and a kindergarten volume
design_condition: The buildings are distributed along the perimeter to create visual transparency between the green corridor and the surrounding streets, structuring the open spaces as a campus.

positive.statement: The three buildings create an interesting spatial transparency and take up the spacious visual references of the garden-city context.
The significant volumes fit comfortably into the context and structure the open spaces in a campus-like manner.
The roof terrace successfully combines the spatial and shady potential of the photovoltaic systems with a roof garden open for school use.
The sensible construction takes comprehensive ecological responsibility into account.
The roof landscape, vertical greenery and diverse vegetation types contribute to sustainability and biodiversity.
The project has been developed in an interesting way and shows an appealing overall quality based on clever urban planning.

negative.statement: A clearer hierarchy of entrances and a more appropriate definition of the arrival side are desirable.
The rectangular playing fields do not fit convincingly with the organic shapes of the green edge.
Distributing the uses across different buildings leaves possible synergies unused and creates considerable additional operational effort.
The large number of entrances makes orientation difficult.
The primary school does not implement the required cluster formation typologically.
The classrooms have an unfavorable ratio of room height to room depth.
The development of the triple gymnasium is very complex and operationally difficult.
The entrances and connections do not sufficiently take school operations into account.
The mezzanine uses have unsuitable room proportions and are unthinkable in this combination.
The kindergarten is spread over two floors and lacks open space for the upper-floor classes.
